newsitem.title: INDIA: India to export 1,000 tonnes tea to Iraq.
newsitem.headline: India to export 1,000 tonnes tea to Iraq.

text.p: India's Tea Board said on Friday it had secured permission to export 1,000 tonnes of black tea to Iraq under the U.N.-supervised "oil-for-food" programme.

A statement from the Tea Board said India's Tata Tea had secured an order to ship 1,000 tonnes of tea "which the company is expected to export in the immediate future. The approval was received by both the Tea Board and Tata Tea today."

The statement did not specify how much Iraqi crude India would receive as part of the tea export deal. Asked how much crude India would receive in lieu of the tea exports, a Tea Board official said: "I cannot tell you that. I am not allowed to speak other than on the clearence of exports of tea to Iraq."

The official, who did not wish to be identified, said permission had been granted by the U.N. Iraq sanctions committee. The contract was signed by Tata Tea and Iraq's Food Stuff Trading Company, the Tea Board statement added.

"In a remarkable breakthrough, India has secured permission to export a thousand tonnes of black tea to Iraq, tea trade with which country virtually came to a standstill since the (1990) war," the Tea Board statement said.
It said India's shipments of tea to Iraq had peaked "in the mid-eighties with about 13,000 tonnes."
